Article.ArticleTitle: Verification of ceftazidime-avibactam and ceftolozane-tazobactam susceptibility testing methods against carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae and Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

Abstract.AbstractText: Ceftazidime-avibactam and ceftolozane-tazobactam are newly approved agents for the treatment of infections caused by multidrug-resistant Gram negative bacteria. Resistance to both agents has been described clinically. Susceptibility testing for either agent is unavailable on automated systems. Our objective was to compare disk diffusion and Etest against standard broth microdilution (BMD) methods for testing ceftazidime-avibactam and ceftolozane-tazobactam against a diverse collection of carbapenem-resistant Enterobacteriaceae (CRE) and Pseudomonas aeruginosa (CRP), respectively. Among 74 ceftazidime-avibactam susceptible and resistant CRE, BMD categorical agreement was higher with Etest (96%) than disk diffusion (72%; P=0.0003). Twenty-eight percent of ceftazidime-avibactam susceptible CRE were classified as resistant by disk diffusion. Results were comparable if resistance was defined genotypically. Among 72 ceftolozane-tazobactam susceptible and resistant CRP, BMD categorical agreement with disk diffusion and Etest was 94% and 96%, respectively; the only errors identified were minor. Our findings demonstrate that Etest measurements of ceftazidime-avibactam and ceftolozane-tazobactam susceptibility are correlated closely with standard BMD methods, suggesting a useful role clinically. On the other hand, disk diffusion measurements over-called ceftazidime-avibactam resistance against CRE. A better understanding of ceftazidime-avibactam interpretive breakpoints is needed before disk diffusion is used routinely in the clinic. Until clinicians and microbiologists understand Etest and disk diffusion performance at their centers, test results should be interpreted cautiously.
